question: The number of years taken for a sum of ₹5,000 to become ₹5,832 at a rate of 16% per annum compounded half-yearly.
solution:
**Given: **

Principal = Rs. 5,000

Amount = Rs. 5,832

Rate = 16% p.a.

**Formula Used:**

Amount = Principal × (1 + (R)/(100))Time

**Calculation: **

When interest compounded annually

R will be half and Time will be doubled.

So,

R = 16/2 = 8% p.a.

Amount = Principal × (1 + (R)/(100))Time

⇒ 5832 = 5000 × (1 + (8)/(100))Time

⇒ (5832)/(5000) = ((108)/(100))^T

⇒ ((729)/(625)) = ((27)/(25))^T

⇒ ((27)/(25))² = ((27)/(25))^T

⇒ Time = 2 years

Because interest is compounded semiannually so, time 2/2 = 1 year.

**∴ ₹5,000 becomes ₹5,832 at a rate of 16% per annum in 1 year when compounded half-yearly**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] **__Shortcut Trick__**Rate = 16% compounded semi-annually, 

R/2 = 16/2 = 8%

Net Rate/Effective Rate,

⇒ 8 + 8 + (8 × 8)/100 = 16.64%

Now,

⇒ 5,000 × 16.64% = 832

Interest = Rs. 832

∴ ₹5,000 becomes ₹5,832 at a rate of 16% per annum in 1 year when compounded half-yearly
